chapter: New York 1930s and New Orleans expatriates
title: First hearing Benny Goodman and Adrian Rollini
summary: Goodman's first records and a Skidmore College dance; Adrian Rollini's pocket reed instrument.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: And George Van Epps and the Guitar Tealers was another big thing in that record to me.
If I'm not mistaken, he still had Frank Troll I think, didn't he?
He might have. I know Charlotte was Frank.

I see, to give you an example, in my hometown, the first time we heard Goodman was at a dance in my hometown, playing for Skidmore College. It just had been booked up there. And all the local musicians were around behind the bandstand. Krupa was with him then, and Frank Frobot, I distinctly remember that that night, Helen Ward. Arthur Rolini was playing tenor sax with him then. I also met Adrian Rolini in those days. I guess some people mentioned it somewhere, but it bears repeating. Adrian was primarily a saxophone player then. He hadn't gone into that trio deal yet. And he made for himself a little reed instrument that he bought the size of a good-sized fountain pen. He had a clip for it, even. He carried it in his pocket, and wherever he went, he felt like sitting in. He could pull this thing out of his pocket like a fountain pen, and by George, sit in and play on it.
That must have been easier to carry than anybody said. You see why he did that.
And it couldn't be more extreme from the saxophone. It was a remarkable thing.
